observed.evidence: Vercel states cron invocations are not automatically retried on failure, overlapping scheduled invocations can occur when a run exceeds its interval, and cron handlers should use idempotent reconciliation plus distributed locking to survive duplicates/overlap.

Vercel runtime logs expose request-level operational evidence such as timestamp, path, status, duration, request identity, deployment and environment; structured logging with stable request IDs makes failures correlatable and machine-readable.

scikit-learn documentation states Brier score and log loss jointly reflect calibration, resolution/discrimination and uncertainty; lower Brier alone does not prove better calibration. Reliability diagrams directly assess calibration, and calibration parameters should be learned on held-out data.

SCoRE (2026) formalizes selective prediction with abstention and finite-sample risk control on the subset of cases a model chooses to trust; its guarantees rely on assumptions such as exchangeability and should not be transferred blindly to drifting football markets.

A 2026 in-play football study on 140 EPL matches reports that pre-match market calibration using Betfair 1X2 and over/under prices was the dominant contributor to predictive accuracy in its live model; the model nearly matched market classification accuracy. Sample size and transferability are limited.

A 2026 odds-conversion study evaluated 90,014 football matches across five bookmakers and reports that bookmaker probabilities require careful margin/bias treatment; simple raw inverse-odds normalization is not necessarily the strongest market-probability baseline.

A 2026 leakage-aware football forecasting paper explicitly centers temporal leakage prevention in pre-match secondary-market modelling, reinforcing that model evaluation must preserve point-in-time feature availability and chronological validation.

API-Football currently lists Pro at 7,500 requests/day and 300 requests/minute, all endpoints and competitions, with daily reset at 00:00 UTC. The provider also exposes pre-match/live odds and emphasizes quota-aware usage.

findings.derived_interpretation: ARGUS should represent each scheduled task as an auditable state machine rather than treating configuration as execution proof. Duplicate/overlapping runs must be survivable by construction.
findings.why_it_matters: A forecasting system cannot be professionally trusted if collection, settlement, calibration or learning jobs silently fail, overlap or double-write.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: On one non-critical research cron only, add a deterministic run_key based on job identity plus intended schedule window, structured start/end/failure events, duplicate detection, and a short-lived lock. Do not alter prediction logic or provider polling.
findings.required_sample_evidence: At least 7 consecutive days and at least 50 intended invocations, including synthetic duplicate/overlap tests in non-production or work-branch execution.
success_metrics: 100% intended runs classified CONFIGURED/DEPLOYED/INVOKED/SUCCEEDED_OR_FAILED/PERSISTED_OR_NOT
duplicate writes = 0 in injected duplicate tests
non-UNKNOWN failure reason on every instrumented failure
no increase in provider calls
findings.failure_condition: Locking causes missed valid runs, instrumentation changes runtime behavior materially, duplicate writes remain possible, or run lineage contains unexplained gaps.
findings.rollback: Remove the research-only lock/ledger wrapper and revert to existing Watchtower/runtime logs; no model state changes.
findings.evidence_level: HIGH for platform behavior; MEDIUM until ARGUS prospective validation

findings.derived_interpretation: ARGUS calibration must be evaluated separately on ALL, ACCEPTED, PRIME and VALUE cohorts, with direct reliability measures rather than Brier/log-loss alone.
findings.why_it_matters: Global calibration can look acceptable while the high-confidence subset used for decisions is systematically overconfident.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Read-only evaluation on frozen, settled predictions: generate equal-frequency reliability bins plus Brier/log-loss for ALL, ACCEPTED, PRIME, VALUE and NO BET cohorts by forward time window. Do not recalibrate or change thresholds yet.
findings.required_sample_evidence: Begin descriptive monitoring at roughly 200 settled accepted selections; require preferably 500+ accepted selections and multiple forward windows before strong trust decisions. These are governance thresholds, not universal statistical laws.
success_metrics: cohort-level sample sizes always shown
reliability curve available alongside proper scores
no hidden aggregation across materially different markets/leagues
confidence/readiness rank does not show systematic overconfidence in accepted tail
findings.failure_condition: Bins are too sparse, confidence cohorts are unstable, or apparent gains disappear under forward-window or market/league stratification.
findings.rollback: Evaluation-only artifact can be removed with zero effect on models or decisions.

findings.derived_interpretation: Before adopting formal conformal thresholds, ARGUS should prove empirically that its own readiness/confidence ranking creates a stable risk-versus-coverage tradeoff on independent forward data.
findings.why_it_matters: NO BET is only valuable if abstaining actually removes disproportionately risky decisions rather than merely shrinking volume.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: For frozen settled predictions, sort by existing readiness/confidence and compute forward-window risk metrics as accepted coverage decreases; report by market and league with bootstrap by match where needed.
findings.required_sample_evidence: Several hundred independent settled matches overall, multiple chronological windows, and enough observations per major market to avoid sparse-tail conclusions.
success_metrics: risk generally falls as coverage becomes stricter
relationship persists across forward windows
no single league/market dominates the effect
tail uncertainty is displayed
findings.failure_condition: Risk is non-monotonic or unstable, gains vanish out of sample, or selectivity merely concentrates exposure in one brittle segment.
findings.rollback: No production threshold changes; discard candidate ranking changes and keep current abstention policy.
findings.evidence_level: HIGH for empirical risk-coverage evaluation; WATCH for formal conformal control

findings.derived_interpretation: ARGUS needs at least one strong market-implied probability baseline that removes bookmaker margin and tests favourite-longshot bias rather than benchmarking against raw inverse odds only.
findings.why_it_matters: If the market baseline is weak or mis-normalized, ARGUS can appear to have edge when it is merely exploiting a poor benchmark.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Offline replay only: compare multiplicative/no-vig normalization, Shin or Power where implementable, and one parsimonious bias-adjusted baseline on frozen opening/closing 1X2 odds. Evaluate log-loss/Brier and calibration, never ROI alone.
findings.required_sample_evidence: At least several thousand historical matches across multiple leagues/bookmakers where timestamped odds are clean; use chronological holdout for any fitted bias parameter.
success_metrics: baseline probabilities sum to one and preserve timestamps/source
fitted methods improve forward proper scores versus simple no-vig
closing-market baseline is stable across leagues/bookmakers
ARGUS comparisons use the strongest validated baseline
findings.failure_condition: Method gains disappear on forward holdout, require unstable bookmaker-specific parameters, or introduce temporal leakage.
findings.rollback: Retain simple multiplicative no-vig baseline and mark advanced de-margining REJECTED for that cohort.

findings.derived_interpretation: A simple interpretable live challenger initialized from pre-match market probabilities may be higher-value than a larger neural architecture, but published evidence is currently too narrow for promotion.
findings.why_it_matters: Market prices aggregate information that a sparse ARGUS live feature set may not capture, especially at kickoff.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Shadow-only replay: initialize a simple intensity/live-state model from frozen kickoff 1X2 and O/U market probabilities, then update only with point-in-time events already proven available. Compare to market-only and current ARGUS baselines.
findings.required_sample_evidence: Target at least 1,000 independent matches across multiple leagues and chronological windows before any promotion discussion; evaluate minute/state predictions clustered by match.
success_metrics: beats current ARGUS and market-only baselines on proper scores in forward windows
calibration remains acceptable
improvement is not concentrated in one league or match phase
findings.failure_condition: Fails to beat market-only baseline, depends on data unavailable point-in-time, or apparent gains vanish when clustering/effective sample size is handled correctly.
findings.rollback: Delete challenger artifact; current live stack unchanged.

findings.derived_interpretation: Exact-score work should remain a baseline competition problem: independent Poisson versus Dixon-Coles-style low-score dependence versus one carefully chosen dependence challenger; no LLM reranking or large model is justified yet.
findings.why_it_matters: Exact score is a high-variance, full-distribution problem where headline top-score accuracy is easy to overfit and difficult to interpret.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Historical chronological replay comparing full score distributions from independent Poisson and Dixon-Coles correction first. Score with multiclass log-loss/RPS-style distribution metrics plus 1X2/O-U coherence derived from the score matrix.
findings.required_sample_evidence: Thousands of matches, league-aware forward windows, and explicit parameter-aging rules.
success_metrics: challenger improves full-distribution proper score out of sample
derived 1X2/O-U probabilities remain coherent
gain persists across more than one league/window
findings.failure_condition: Only top-1 exact-score hit rate improves, calibration worsens, or gains disappear outside training leagues.

findings.derived_interpretation: API-Football Pro remains sufficient for research growth unless measured evidence shows quota saturation is causing loss of high-value snapshots. Optimization should maximize information per request before upgrading.
findings.why_it_matters: More calls do not equal better forecasts; quota pressure can encourage redundant polling and reduce reliability.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Read-only quota accounting on existing responses: classify calls by endpoint, cache-hit/miss, candidate match relevance, and whether the call produced a new decision-relevant fact. No extra calls.
findings.required_sample_evidence: At least 7 days covering multiple match-load profiles, including one high-load day.
success_metrics: daily/minute quota truth reconciled
redundant calls identified
critical snapshots are not missed
upgrade decision based on measured unmet information need
findings.failure_condition: Instrumentation itself increases calls or cannot reconcile provider truth with local accounting.
findings.rollback: Remove local accounting layer; provider plan remains unchanged.
findings.evidence_level: HIGH for provider limits; MEDIUM for ARGUS utilization efficiency

rejected.idea: Deploy a larger live transformer or LLM-based exact-score reranker now
rejected.reason: Novelty does not address ARGUS's current evidence debt. Point-in-time live data, calibration, market baselines and execution truth must be proven first. LLMs are not inherently calibrated probability engines.

rejected.idea: Copy published live betting ROI into ARGUS decision rules
rejected.reason: Published simulations are non-transferable without independent replication, transaction/market details, timestamp integrity and forward validation. Proper scores and CLV/market benchmarks outrank short-term ROI claims.

rejected.idea: Treat formal conformal guarantees as immediately valid for football leagues/markets
rejected.reason: Exchangeability/group-stability assumptions are not guaranteed under football drift. Empirical ARGUS risk-coverage must be stable first.

rejected.idea: Upgrade API-Football solely to accelerate learning
rejected.reason: Pro already provides 7,500 requests/day and all endpoints/competitions. Upgrade only if measured high-value data is being missed after optimization.

handoff.execute_next: Instrument one non-critical research cron with idempotent run identity, overlap protection and durable failure lineage, then verify CONFIGURED -> DEPLOYED -> INVOKED -> SUCCEEDED/FAILED -> PERSISTED/NOT_PERSISTED prospectively.
handoff.why_now: Control Plane truth is prerequisite evidence for every downstream learning, calibration, settlement and data-acquisition claim; Vercel documents duplicate/overlap risks and no automatic cron retry.
handoff.expected_benefit: Eliminate silent/duplicate cron ambiguity, improve failure memory and make future research evidence trustworthy.
handoff.evidence_level: HIGH platform evidence, MEDIUM ARGUS-specific until prospectively validated
handoff.minimum_test: One non-critical research cron, 7 days, >=50 intended invocations, synthetic duplicate/overlap test, zero model/provider-polling changes.
success_metrics: complete run lineage
zero duplicate writes
100% instrumented failures have non-UNKNOWN reason
no added provider calls
handoff.failure_condition: Runtime behavior changes, legitimate runs are suppressed, duplicate writes occur, or lineage has unexplained gaps.
handoff.proof_required: Prospective evidence across seven days plus sampled cross-check against Vercel runtime logs.
risk_leakage_risks: instrumentation must not mutate prediction state
do not infer success from config alone
do not rewrite historical run state
do not let duplicate live states count as independent matches
handoff.rollback: Remove research-only wrapper/lock and keep existing Watchtower/runtime logs; no model state touched.
watch: selected-case risk-vs-coverage before formal conformal thresholds
market-anchored live challenger only after point-in-time event proof
do_not_do: no API upgrade without measured need
data_to_acquire_next: frozen settled predictions by decision cohort
provider quota truth on existing responses
handoff.next_research_question: After Control Plane truth is proven, does existing ARGUS readiness/confidence produce stable monotonic risk reduction as accepted coverage decreases across independent forward windows and markets?
blockers: cron lineage not yet prospectively validated
selected-cohort calibration sample may still be sparse
live event point-in-time completeness not yet proven
